minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 6, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:00 p.m., on July 6, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on July 01, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title “Council Member.”

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:15 p.m.)
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:42 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht
Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was no Closed Session business this evening.

INVOCATION: Mayor Schlicht

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

City Council Minutes  1  July 6, 2015
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim July 2015 as Recreation & Parks Month

  Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to Director of Recreation and Community
  Services Mark Nix and recreation department staff.

P2.  Certificate of Appreciation to Mended Hearts for Their Donation of Four Automated
  External Defibrillators (AED) to the City’s Recreation Facilities

  Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay and Mayor Schlicht presented the certificate of
  appreciation to President Dennis Galloway and the Board of Directors of Mended Hearts,
  Chapter 216.

P3.  Proclamation on the 40th Anniversary of AYSO Region 84

  Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to Dave Selecky, Regional Commissioner for
  AYSO Region 84.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Thuy Le, Aliso Viejo: presented information on My Open Road, a new app designed to help
people reduce their carbon footprint with alternative, efficient means of transportation.

Chuck McCollough, M.V.: invited the City Council Members to upcoming Chamber of Commerce
events including the monthly mixer, ribbon cutting ceremonies and weekly meetings.

David Allen, M.V.: on behalf of the Mission Viejo Activities Committee (MVAC) he thanked City
staff for their hard work and the City Council Members for attending the 4th of July Street Faire.
He also thanked all of the MVAC volunteers who made the event possible.

Tom Sorenson, M.V.: provided an update on the Nadadores fundraising efforts for the aquatics
center renovation.

Alan and Sheri Isaacs, and Josh Preevy, M.V.: expressed concern with loud parties and fireworks
on the fire road in the Pacific Hills neighborhood. There have also been car break-ins and items
stolen from a garage. They suggested that the fire road should be closed after 10:00 p.m. and that
permit parking is instituted to help with this ongoing problem.

Amelya (Stacy) Harrison, M.V.: discussed the proliferation of illegal fireworks in Mission Viejo
and stated that she feels the need to stay home on the 4th of July to protect her home. She stated
that the police do not respond when called and she asked the Council to consider raising the fine
for setting-off illegal fireworks.

City Council Minutes  2  July 6, 2015
 Gail Reavis, M.V.: discussed her possible $100,000 donation to the Nadadores for naming the dive
platform after her deceased husband. She stated that she is waiting for the City and the Nadadores
to be on the same page about naming rights before she can make a donation.

Casey Cooper, Ph.D., M.V.: reminded the Council that on June 15 she shared her personal
concerns with the Mayor's pervasive pattern of behavior and she noted that the Mayor has not
responded to her comments or emails. Ms. Cooper sated that the City needs a new Mayor and she
asked what the Council is waiting for.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: suggested that the City institute a report card based on specific criteria
to evaluate the efforts and effectiveness of individual City Council Members and the City Manager.
He also asked the Council 10 questions on matters that concern him.

Anna Warner, M.V.: stated that city inspectors issued building permits for a house that violated
numerous building standards and she asked the Council for a response.

Mayor Schlicht responded that this is not a matter for the City Council and that Mrs. Warner needs
to hire an attorney.

Lin Marelic, M.V.: thanked the Community Services Commission for listening to residents' issues
with proposed changes to landscaping in the Aegean Hills neighborhoods. She also thanked
Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay for meeting with the residents and taking their
recommendations into consideration.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 12, 13, 18, and 26 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths asked Mayor Schlicht why she pulls so many items at every Council
meeting. He noted that she can make a phone call to have her questions answered.

Mayor Schlicht responded that she reads the agenda items thoroughly and she has questions on the
check registers. She stated that there are some items that need discussion, especially three
contracts on tonight’s agenda, and the questions should be asked in a public meeting for
transparency.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  3  July 6, 2015
 1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 15, 2015, as presented.

City Council Minutes  5  July 6, 2015

  Authorized the City Manager to enter into an agreement with the City of Newport Beach

City Council Minutes  6  July 6, 2015
   California Edison (SCE) Service Area to the City of Newport Beach in exchange for

  Adopted Resolution 15-33 Providing for the Revision to the CalPERS Special

27.  Partnership Agreement with Pacific Symphony for Symphony in the Cities Summer

  Approved Partnership Agreement with Pacific Symphony for Symphony in the Cities

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated June 5, 2015 in the Amount of $426,679.10

  Mayor Schlicht asked about a bill paid to the County of Ventura for Gartner Core Research
  in the amount of $8,600. She also asked about the effectiveness of banners to publicize
  City events and activities.

  Director Dyas and Assistant City Manager Rattay provided responses.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury

  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register Dated June 12, 2015 in the Amount of $1,401,247.68

  Mayor Schlicht asked about payment to Aegis ITS for battery backup and whether or not
  it has anything to do with a power failure several years ago when the traffic signal backups
  did not work.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon confirmed that there is a continuing effort to
  upgrade the signal backup batteries.

  Mayor Schlicht also inquired about a payment to Dudek for professional services for parks.

City Council Minutes  7  July 6, 2015
   Operations Manager Jerry Hill noted that the City hired a professional tree trimmer to train
  staff and contract personnel after the City received some complaints about possible
  conflicts with bird nesting.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury

  ABSENT:  None

12.  Playground, Parkland, and Facilities Safety Inspection Services

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1) award contract
  for the subject services to Jamey Clark, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015, through June

  Jamey Clark, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015, through June 30, 2016, in an amount not
  to exceed $165,000.00 pending adoption of the 2015-2017 budget by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13.  Playground, Parkland, and Facility Infrastructure Maintenance and Repair

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht stated that there is a conflict of interest when you have inspection work
  done by the same contractor that is going to do the repair.

  Director Rattay noted that staff meets every week and has a deliberate process for oversight
  of the contracts.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht to reject the recommended action and award a contract to
  Tom Bistline Construction. The motion died for lack of a second.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1) award
  contract for the subject services to Jamey Clark, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015, through
  June 30, 2017, in the amount of $734,000.00; and (2) authorize issuance of a purchase

City Council Minutes  8  July 6, 2015
   order to Jamey Clark, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015, through June 30, 2016, in an
  amount not to exceed $367,000.00 pending adoption of the 2015-2017 budget by City
  Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

18.  Annual Graffiti Removal, Steam Cleaning, Painting, and Sealing Services

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report
  and answered the City Council Members questions.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1) reject all bids
  received for the Annual Graffiti Removal, Steam Cleaning, Painting, and Sealing Services;
  (2) approve the Third Amendment to the existing contract with Bonanza Steam Cleaning,
  Inc. for the two-month period; and (3) issue new purchase order to Bonanza Steam
  Cleaning, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $12,000.00 for the extended contract term.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

26.  Legislative Advocacy and Government Relations Services

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht expressed concern with lobbyists coming between residents and

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  the Professional Services Agreement with Townsend Public Affairs(A15-48) for State
  legislative advocacy and government relations services for a total not to exceed the amount

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  9  July 6, 2015
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

35.  Capistrano Valley High School and Coronado Homes Neighborhood Parking Issues

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in favor of maintaining the parking permit program from 9:30 a.m. to
  5:30 p.m. and/or against parking along Avery Parkway: Scott McClellan, M.V.; Delbert
  Mortenson, M.V.; Scott Moor, M.V; Don Wilder, M.V.; Sandra Hull, M.V.; Jake
  Jacobson, M.V.; Michael-Alese Ramsey, M.V.; Holly Lawyer, M.V.; Al Holguin, M.V.;
  Molly Mathes, M.V.; Jerry Jones, M.V.; and Marlene Sais, M.V.
  Chad Smith, newly appointed Principal of Capistrano Valley High School, M.V.:
  expressed the school's willingness to find a solution to the problem by supporting both the
  neighbors and the school community.

  The following spoke in opposition to the current hours and/or to finding alternative
  solutions: Scott McKernan, M.V. (shared a video of students and cars in the neighborhood);
  Doreen McKernan, M.V.; Anthony Accetta, M.V.; Stacy Joyce, M.V.; Christina Lee,
  M.V.; and Sue Dennis, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in favor of maintaining the parking permit
  program from 9:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. and/or against parking along Avery Parkway: Anide
  Johnson, M.V.; Mary Galvin, M.V.; James Vandenbergh, M.V.; Ron St. Jean, M.V.; and
  Sandra Hull, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in favor of returning the parking restrictions to
  the previous hours (9:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.): Julie Muller, M.V.; Barbara Schafer, M.V.;
  Susan Carroll, M.V.; Kelly Brewer, M.V.; Gretchen Mars, M.V.; Karen Wise, M.V.; and
  Dorothy Mowry, M.V.

  The City Council Members made comments and asked questions of staff.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to (1) maintain the
  current hours of Schools Days Only 9:30 am to 5:30 pm; (2) maintain "No Parking" along
  Avery Parkway; (3) place a minimum of two-year moratorium on the Coronado
  Neighborhood permit parking hours to prevent this issue from being repeatedly revisited;
  and (4) direct staff and public safety to work in conjunction with Capistrano Valley High
  School Principal Smith, the Capistrano Unified School District (CUSD,) the PTA, and
  homeowners to come up with a long-term solution to the parking issues.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  10  July 6, 2015
 STAFF REPORTS

36.  Update on Drought Tolerant Response Program and Community Service
  Commission Meeting of May 20, 2015

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay staff report and presented
  a detailed plan for each park in the Aegean Hills neighborhood.

  The following spoke in support of the proposed plan for moving forward as outlined in the
  staff report: Joseph Tully, M.V. and John Burus, M.V.
  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  appropriate $12,000 for the Aegean Hills drought tolerant landscape plan and return to the
  Community Services Commission for review and approval.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Bucknum
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

29.  Award design contract for the Marguerite Aquatics Complex to Aquatic Design
  Group

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Jim Montrella, M.V.: expressed his and the Nadadores support for the hiring of Aquatic
  Design Group.

  The City Council Members asked questions of staff.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to award a
  contract for the design and engineering services to Aquatic Design Group (A15-49) in an
  amount not to exceed $598,500 and issue a purchase order; and (2) direct staff to look at
  the 15% markup on some of the reimbursable expenses.

  Mayor Schlicht stated that she would prefer that the City issue a RFP. She noted that she
  reached out to another design company that could potentially save the City money but she
  could see that her colleagues were not interested in discussing that.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  11  July 6, 2015
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

28.  Adoption of the 2015-17 Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed the proposed changes to the salary classifications
  and asked that staff create an Excel spreadsheet that outlines what Mission Viejo pays
  employees compared to six surrounding cities.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve (1) Resolution 15-34 Adopting a Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for 2015-
  17 and Appropriating Funds for FY 15-16 only, and (2) Resolution 15-35, Amending the
  City's Salary Schedule and Establishing Salary Ranges for Authorized Job Classifications.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

30.  Optional Agreed Upon Audit Procedures

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented staff report.

  The City Council Members asked questions and made recommendations. By consensus,
  the Council directed Mayor Schlicht and Mayor Pro Tem Raths to follow-up with the
  auditors.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

31.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report/AB1217 (Daly)

  Council Member Sachs presented the report and requested that the City Council adopt the
  proposed resolution which will put AB1217 to rest.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the OCFA is out of control and that the Board of
  Directors is finally getting the bigger picture.

City Council Minutes  12  July 6, 2015
   Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  adopt Resolution 15-36 Approving the Third Amendment to the Amended Orange County
  Fire Authority JPA Agreement and authorizing execution of the Amendment.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 32.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Given the late hour, Council Member Ury deferred his report to the next City Council
  Meeting.

 33.  Voting Delegate and Alternate(s) for the 2015 League of California Cities Annual
  Conference

  Mayor Schlicht appointed Council Member Sachs as the voting delegate and herself and
  Council Member Bucknum as alternates for the League of California Cities Conference
  Annual Business Meeting on October 2, 2015.

 34.  Update from Economic Development Committee and Agreement for Professional
  Services for Economic Development Implementation – Kosmont Companies

  The City Council received a verbal update from Mayor Pro Tem Raths and Council
  Member Sachs on recent Economic Development Committee activity.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve
  an agreement with Kosmont Companies from July 7, 2015n to June 30, 2016, in an amount
  not to exceed $40,000 for economic development implementation services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 37.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  13  July 6, 2015
   The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at recent events including the Capistrano
Valley High School graduation, the DAWG Walk, and the 4th of July Street Faire. She announced
that a small group of people in the City are systematically attacking and slandering good people
including herself, her husband and her children. Not only that but they've made false accusations
about people that she works for and organizations that she is involved with. She stated that this
group uses a printed blog cloaked as a newspaper, a website, social media and anonymous fliers
to spread their propaganda and misinformation. Council Member Bucknum noted that the time
that staff spends answering questions that are not based on reality costs the City money and she
wants to protect taxpayers from these expenses. She feels that this group is attempting to destroy
people's reputations, businesses, and non-profit organizations and that the Council has to stand up
against the bullying. Council Member Bucknum further declared that the Mayor perpetuates this
and it is extremely disappointing because the Council Members are not supposed to spread rumors,
they should stop them. She stated that Mayor Schlicht is having trouble gathering consensus and
speaks without the authority of the City Council and it is becoming an embarrassment. Council
Member Bucknum noted that she is questioning the Mayor's leadership as are residents and people
should consider the source of information. If it's anonymous it's because someone isn't proud
enough to put their name behind something that is supposedly factual.

Council Member Sachs

Directing his comments to Orange County Fire Authority and Sheriff's Department representatives
in the audience, Council Member Sachs asked them to look into comments that were made earlier
in the evening regarding activity on a fire road and illegal fireworks. He asked that the residents’
concerns be addressed. Council Member Sachs stated each Council Member has the right to vote
how they see fit. Others may not appreciate how in-artful their colleague is in presenting an idea
or opinion but they should take into consideration that everyone on the Council has but one vote
and the same ability and opportunity to say what they want to try and persuade others to their
side. He noted that although he doesn’t agree with a lot of votes that are taken, once they are done
he moves on to the next thing. Council Member Sachs stated that he really finds it curious that
these matters have to be discussed in public and he recommended that Council Members go to
each other first and see if they can come to some resolution.

Council Member Ury

38.  Purchase of Smart Technology Controllers for City of Mission Viejo Neighborhood
  Parks

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

City Council Minutes  14  July 6, 2015
   Joseph Tully, M.V.: expressed his support for the proposal.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, (1)
  Appropriate $195,000 for the purchase and installation of the Smart Technology
  Controllers for 38 City neighborhood parks from the General Fund. The purchase is to be
  funded by using rebate funds obtained from the Metropolitan Water District, and $115,525
  from the General Fund to complete the purchase; (2) authorize City staff to process a
  contract and issue a purchase order to Signature Control Systems and issue a purchase order
  in an amount not to exceed $195,000; and (3) proclaim July as “Smart Irrigation Month”
  in Mission Viejo.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Due to his schedule, Mayor Pro Tem Raths asked that the Mayor give his position on the water ad
hoc committee to Council Member Bucknum. He thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee
for all that they did on the 4th of July to make the day a success. Mayor Pro Tem Raths then read
a prepared statement on the slanderous attacks that he and his family have recently received from
a small group of activists. He asked the Council Members to raise their hand if they repudiate this
attack on him. He said that people can come after him all they want but please leave his family
out of it.

Mayor Schlicht

Mayor Schlicht stated that she is the same person that she was when she was selected as Mayor
and when she was first elected six years ago. She noted that she has been interested in politics
since she was 10 years old and she doesn’t hold grudges. Mayor Schlicht stated that she will not
be intimidated into something that she is not or changing the way she votes. She believes that she
represents the silent majority and she does not pander to special interests. She discussed the
Economic Coalition’s position on certain topics and stated that she has voiced her concerns over
that. Mayor Schlicht stated that there is a minority point of view in the audience and she is not
going to succumb to their hostility. Changing the subject, she discussed her interest in creating a
youth center where kids can hang out and she announced that the Saddleback Republican
Assembly will hold a program called “Water 101” presented by William Hunt on Sunday, July 12
at 3:00 p.m. Kids Factory will also be starting up for the summer and goes through August 28. She
also expressed kudos to the USA women’s soccer team who beat Japan 5-2 and she commended
Mission Viejo High School softball player Taylor McQuillin who has won various awards for her
terrific softball fast pitch. Mayor Schlicht stated that she has kept to her pledge as a voice of reason
for open government, fiduciary responsibility, demanding transparency and never accepting
contributions that attempt to bias her vote. She concluded by reading the patriotic speech that she
